Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables' results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mike Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Brooks, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Harlan.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter:

First, we raised our full-year capacity addition guidance to 2.3 to 2.6 gigawatts of new net capacity online, reflecting stronger construction progress and favorable grid queues, with a robust 48-gigawatt gross development pipeline positioning us for sustained growth.

Second, we achieved record storage deployments of 450 megawatts over 1.8 gigawatt-hours in the quarter, alongside key hybrid project milestones that are enhancing our dispatchable clean energy offerings.

Third, revenue hit a record $1.45 billion, up 52 percent year-over-year, with earnings growth underscoring the strength of our segments and policy tailwinds.

Fourth, we executed $850 million in capital recycling through asset sales, unlocking proceeds to fuel our high-return pipeline.

Fifth, PPA pricing trends remained constructive amid extensions that added significant backlog value at premium rates.

Sixth, broader market trends like solar cost deflation and storage acceleration are aligning perfectly with our strategy.

Now, I will turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Mike. We are very pleased with our financial performance in Q2. Revenue was $1.45 billion, a 52 percent increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 28.4 percent, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $350 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $162 million, or $0.92 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Diving deeper into the revenue and earnings growth, this marks our ninth straight quarter of accelerating top-line expansion, fueled by a 65 percent surge in module shipments to 8.2 gigawatt-direct-current and strong contributions from energy storage and services. Solar PV modules drove 72 percent of revenue at $1.04 billion, up 61 percent, with 5.1 gigawatts shipped at firm average selling prices of $0.28 per watt thanks to our premium N-type TOPCon tech. BESS contributed 18 percent at $261 million, up 112 percent on 2.4 gigawatt-hours deployed, while services and hydrogen added $145 million.

Regionally, North America led with $785 million, up 78 percent on IRA credits worth $220 million; Europe $412 million up 42 percent; APAC $174 million up 15 percent; and rest of world $79 million up 35 percent. This balance shielded us from global ASP pressures.

On the earnings side, adjusted EBITDA reached $285 million with a 19.7 percent margin, up 210 basis points, driven by gross margin expansion to 28.4 percent from scale at our 25-gigawatt TOPCon capacity running at 92 percent utilization and polysilicon costs down to $8.5 per kilogram. OpEx discipline kept SG&A at 7.2 percent of revenue, with R&D up 15 percent to $85 million focused on perovskite tandems. Cash flow was robust at $320 million operating, generating $1.2 billion year-to-date free cash flow.

Turning to capital recycling, a core value driver, we closed $850 million in sales across 650 megawatts, exceeding guidance and funding our full-year capex. Highlights included the $550 million U.S. solar portfolio sale to I Squared Capital at $1.38 million per megawatt and a 14.8 percent IRR, the $210 million European wind recap to Allianz at 13.2 percent IRR, and the $90 million Australian BESS flip at 15.5 percent IRR. These generated $720 million net proceeds, with multiples around 9 times EBITDA amid strong infrastructure demand and IRA transferability.

On PPA pricing trends and extensions, new solar pricing compressed to $24 per megawatt-hour unscubbed, down 8 percent year-over-year on module costs below $0.25 per watt-peak and hyperscaler demand, but our hybrids hit sub-$20 per megawatt-hour LCOE. Wind held at $32 to $38 per megawatt-hour. Regionally, ERCOT shone at $28 to $32 per megawatt-hour, California at $26 per megawatt-hour, Europe auctions at 42 euros per megawatt-hour. We executed 1.2 gigawatts of extensions at 18 percent uplifts to $42 per megawatt-hour blended, like the Rattlesnake Solar 10-year deal at $48 per megawatt-hour, adding $1.8 billion to backlog via retrofits and repowers.

We're guiding Q3 revenue at $1.6 to $1.7 billion and full-year $6.4 to $6.6 billion, with EPS $1.25 to $1.30.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Brooks for an update on our project pipeline.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jordan. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 48 gigawatts gross under development, 11 gigawatts in advanced stages, and 3.5 gigawatts shovel-ready. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, targeting 8 to 10 gigawatts annual additions through fiscal 2027 at 20 to 25 percent conversion. Year-to-date, 1.1 gigawatts online puts us 15 percent ahead.

U.S. represents 55 percent at 26.5 gigawatts total, 6.2 in advanced, with IRA tailwinds like $12 billion in PTC/ITC transfers and 10 gigawatts solar-plus-storage in ERCOT and CAISO. Europe at 25 percent, 12 gigawatts total, focuses on REPowerEU auctions at 50 euros per megawatt-hour and 4 gigawatts offshore. Asia-Pacific 15 percent, 7.2 gigawatts with India partnerships; emerging five percent on green hydrogen.

We're prioritizing hybrids for 70 percent of additions, capturing 20 to 30 percent higher capacity factors; repowering $500 million for 2 gigawatts; and M&A like 1.5 gigawatts year-to-date. This supports 15 gigawatts COD by end fiscal 2027, growing our portfolio to 27 gigawatts at 20 percent CAGR, with 85 percent of fiscal 2024 additions contracted at $45 per megawatt-hour.

Next, Dr. Vasquez will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Taylor. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future. The development of our SolStor hybrid platform is expected to have transformative impact on our future projects, lifting IRRs and enabling firm power.

On storage deployment, Q2 was a record with 450 megawatts over 1.8 gigawatt-hours commissioned, year-to-date 820 megawatts over 3.3 gigawatt-hours, 25 percent ahead of 1.8 gigawatt over 7.2 gigawatt-hours full-year guide. Flagship ERCOT ThunderHub, 200 megawatts over 800 megawatt-hours with Fluence Gridstack Pro and our OptiDispatch AI, generated over $12 million from arbitrage and reserves at 85 percent utilization. CAISO Central Valley Stack 150 megawatts over 450 megawatt-hours secures RA payments; UK Drax 100 megawatts over 400 megawatt-hours captures capacity auctions.

We're shifting to eight-hour duration at 70 percent of deployments, with pack costs at $140 per kilowatt-hour and 22 percent EPC margins. Backlog 3.2 gigawatts over 12.8 gigawatt-hours, including Microsoft 300 megawatts over 1.2 gigawatt-hours PPA. LDES pilots like 50 megawatts over 500 megawatt-hours iron-air show 85 percent efficiency.

For hybrids, 60 percent of 12-gigawatt pipeline, Q2 NTP on 650 megawatts solar plus 250 megawatts storage: California Desert Rose 300 megawatts-ac First Solar plus Powin; Texas Panhandle wind-solar-Tesla; Australian Kidston Phase 2. Operational fleet 1.2 gigawatts delivered $85 million EBITDA at 38 percent capacity factors, diversified across energy, capacity, ancillary via SolaraGrid.

CapEx $450 to $500 million H2, fully funded, with 95 percent hedge ratio.

And now, Raj Patel will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon footprint to near-zero through Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions tracking, improving energy efficiency across operations, and promoting responsible resource management like water recycling in solar sites. We are also actively involved in community engagement, supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability, such as biodiversity programs around wind farms and workforce training in clean tech hubs. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense, enhancing our social license and attracting ESG-focused capital.

I'll now turn the call back to Mike Harlan for closing remarks.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, Raj. In closing, we are confident that Solara Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Mike Harlan:
Thanks, John. The regulatory landscape remains supportive overall, particularly with the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act providing uncapped PTC and ITC incentives, including domestic content bonuses that we've fully leveraged across 85 percent of our U.S. projects. We've navigated BOEM fast-tracks for offshore permitting and ERCOT's reliability standards effectively. In Europe, REPowerEU auctions and national targets are accelerating tenders despite some TSO delays, while we're mitigating risks through localized manufacturing in Germany. Asia-Pacific benefits from India's 500-gigawatt goal and Australia's VRE mandates. Election-year uncertainties in the U.S. could introduce permitting slips, but our advanced queues and partnerships de-risk that. Overall, policy alignment is strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Emily. Integration challenges like curtailment, grid constraints, and cycle life are front and center, but our approach via DC-coupled hybrids and AI optimization is proving effective. For instance, OptiDispatch software enables real-time bidding across markets, achieving 92 percent round-trip efficiency and 85 percent utilization in ERCOT. We've standardized on LFP from CATL and BYD for cost stability under IRA credits, with eight-hour durations now dominant to match duck curves. Pilots in LDES with Form Energy address multi-day needs. Across our 1.2-gigawatt operational hybrids, capacity factors hit 38 percent, with revenue stacking from arbitrage, RA, and FCAS. Software like SolaraGrid aggregates VPPs, reducing intermittency risks by 25 percent in capture prices.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with GreenWave Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Mike Harlan:
Thanks, Sarah, great question. Let me dive into the key market trends shaping our industry and how they're directly influencing our trajectory here at Solara Renewables. As you know, we're a leader in integrated solar-plus-storage solutions, with over 15 gigawatts of utility-scale projects deployed globally since our IPO.

Solar PV cost deflation and deployment acceleration lead the way. Global additions hit 447 gigawatts-dc in 2023, up 55 percent year-over-year per BloombergNEF, on track for 510 gigawatts in 2024. Module prices dropped 50 percent to $0.15 per watt for TOPCon, supercharging our LCOE below $25 per megawatt-hour and locking 3.2 gigawatts PPAs 12 percent above guidance, growing backlog to $12.4 billion.

Hybridization with storage is transformative. Dispatchables are 65 percent of our pipeline; storage added 76 gigawatts over 200 gigawatt-hours last year at under $100 per kilowatt-hour pack. Our SolStor platform wins 80 percent of U.S. RFPs, with Q3 commissions capturing $45 per megawatt-hour spreads and lifting EBITDA margins to 32 percent, raising FY24 guide to $1.8 to $2.0 billion.

Policy tailwinds differentiate regions. U.S. IRA funneled $110 billion, qualifying our Georgia fab for bonuses on 8-gigawatt backlog. Europe awarded 50 gigawatts post-REPowerEU; we're pivoting to agrivoltaics. Asia sees China's curtailment ease enabling 250 gigawatts, with our Vietnam offshore hybrids.

Emerging like green hydrogen—CAPEX down 20 percent to $800 per kilowatt—and perovskites targeting 30 percent efficiency add upside, with $250 million investment. AI via GridSync cuts curtailment 15 percent.

Challenges like BOS inflation and rates are managed with $4.2 billion liquidity. We're expanding U.S. manufacturing and partnering like with Orsted, validating 20 to 25 percent revenue CAGR and 11 percent ROIC expansion.

Sarah, does that cover it, or want specifics on a region?

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Mike Harlan for any closing remarks.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Solara Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
